title: Section realization of coefficient scalar extension
statement: For commutative condensed rings R,S and a ring-object map a with exact internal scalar extension on every scheme, and every scheme Z, the actual scalar extension satisfies CoefficientScalarSectionRealization(a,Z) [def-sfb-coefficient-scalar-tensor-realization-data]. Thus the normalized ordinary and derived scalar adjunctions, generalized pure-generator formula, ordinary scalar monoidal constraint, signed flat-term K-flat totalization square, and identification with the specified internal derived scalar tensorator all hold. No geometric morphism, boundedness, or finiteness assumption is involved.

proof.text: Apply internal_section_scalar_adjunction to the actual coefficient map. This supplies the normalized section pair, restriction and ordinary extension comparisons, their identity and generator formulas, and their ordinary Hom equation. For its internal adjunction, use leftAdjointUniq from the native derived extension/comap adjunction. The native derived unit formula follows from the levelwise exact adjunction and the derived-to-exact factorization isomorphisms. Compare the two unit formulas and use injectivity of the native Hom equivalence to prove that the uniqueness isomorphism carries the internal computation counit to coefficientInternalScalarComplex. Whisker this uniqueness isomorphism with the derived section equivalence and compose with the existing derived scalar comparison. Substitution proves the scalar representative square, and naturality of the Hom equivalences proves the specified derived Hom equation.

Apply scalarExtension_constraint_coherence to the actual section coefficient map. Its tensor and unit isomorphisms define a CoreMonoidal structure on the functor with the prescribed changeOfRings objects and maps; its naturality and three coherence equations verify the CoreMonoidal laws. The object equalities of the normalized scalar pair give a natural isomorphism to its extension functor. Transport the monoidal structure through this isomorphism. Cancel the equality-transport maps in the pure scalar generator and transport the pure tensor along the equality isomorphisms. The existing arbitrary-scalar formula of the constraint data gives exactly the required generator formula.

Form the natural isomorphism on internal derived pairs by composing the inverse section tensor comparison, the inverse scalar extension comparison, the fixed internalScalarTensorIso, the section tensor comparison for S and the product of the scalar extension comparisons. Precomposition by the product section equivalence is fully faithful, so take its inverse image to define the section derived tensor isomorphism t. The map/preimage identity and cancellation of the scalar and tensor comparison isomorphisms prove the required internal identification equation.

Apply coefficientScalarTensorRepresentative to the constructed ordinary scalar comparison, derived scalar comparison, ordinary monoidal structure and derived tensor isomorphism, with the generator, scalar-computation and internal identification equations just proved. This gives the remaining signed flat-term K-flat representative equation. Assemble these witnesses and equations with the unchanged restriction normalization and ordinary and derived Hom formulas to prove every conjunct of CoefficientScalarSectionRealization.
